questions.q: Why does this lesson say a list of desired outcomes with no sequencing isn't actually a roadmap yet?
options: Because a roadmap must be exactly 12 months long
Because sequencing is where enterprise-architecture dependencies -- like resolving master data ownership before building an integration -- actually get applied; an unsequenced list is just a backlog
Because roadmaps are not allowed to include more than three items
Because only Salesforce-only initiatives can appear on a roadmap
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes a roadmap from a backlog specifically by its sequencing -- real-time ERP integration might depend on resolved master data ownership, legacy retirement might depend on a strangler-fig migration reaching a certain point, and so on.

questions.q: What does this lesson say a Salesforce-only view of roadmap planning risks missing?
options: Nothing -- a Salesforce-only view is always sufficient for enterprise roadmap planning
Cross-system dependencies, such as a planned Salesforce feature depending on an ERP upgrade scheduled on a different team's own roadmap
The need to ever use a sandbox
The need for a System Architect to be involved at all
questions.explain: The lesson warns that cross-system dependencies -- like a Salesforce feature depending on an ERP team's own separately-scheduled upgrade -- are invisible from a Salesforce-only view and need to be made explicit, often through landscape diagrams.

questions.q: Per this lesson, which sandbox type copies metadata plus a sample of production data, selected via a sandbox template, suited to testing scenarios needing realistic data?
options: Developer sandbox
Developer Pro sandbox
Partial Copy sandbox
Full Copy sandbox
questions.explain: A Partial Copy sandbox copies metadata plus a sample of production data chosen via a sandbox template, making it suited to testing scenarios like user acceptance testing that need realistic (though not complete) data.

questions.q: Which sandbox type does this lesson describe as replicating all production metadata and data, with the longest refresh interval of the four types?
options: Developer sandbox
Full Copy sandbox
Partial Copy sandbox
Developer Pro sandbox
questions.explain: A Full Copy sandbox replicates all production metadata and data and has the longest refresh interval of the four sandbox types, making it suited to final UAT, performance testing, and troubleshooting production issues.

questions.q: What risk does this lesson say a roadmap takes on if it plans a major release without accounting for a Full Copy sandbox's refresh interval?
options: No risk -- sandbox refresh intervals never affect release timing
Discovering too late that the environment needed for final testing isn't actually ready on the schedule the roadmap assumed
Automatically triggering a security breach
Losing all production data permanently
questions.explain: Because Full Copy sandboxes have the longest refresh interval of the four types, a roadmap that ignores this when scheduling final testing risks discovering the testing environment isn't ready when the plan assumed it would be.
